committee_name.text: Peripheral and Central Nervous System Drugs Advisory Committee (PCNS)

quote.quote: This NDA was discussed at an Advisory Committee meeting of the PCNS Committee on March 30, 2022.

meeting_date.text: The PCNS committee met twice for this NDA: initially on March 30, 2022, and reconvened on September 7, 2022.

quote.quote: the PCNS Advisory Committee was reconvened on September 7, 2022

recommendation.text: At the first meeting (March 30, 2022) the committee voted 6-4 (NO) that the available data were not sufficient to establish that AMX0035 is effective in ALS. After the applicant submitted additional confirmatory-evidence analyses, the committee was reconvened (September 7, 2022) and voted 7-2 (one member absent) in favor of approval.

quote.quote: The Committee voted 7-2 (one member absent) in favor of approval.

linkages.concern: At the March 30, 2022 meeting, the PCNS committee voted 6-4 that the available data (the single controlled trial AMX3500 plus the open-label extension) were not sufficient to establish that AMX0035 is effective in the treatment of ALS.
linkages.change: Following the committee meeting, the applicant submitted a major amendment containing additional analyses intended to serve as confirmatory evidence (additional survival analyses, an individual responder analysis, and Alzheimer's-disease biomarker findings), which extended the review timeline by three months; the PCNS committee was then reconvened on September 7, 2022 and voted 7-2 in favor of approval, and the drug was approved.

concern_quote.quote: The Committee voted 6-4 that the available data were not sufficient to establish a conclusion that AMX0035 is effective in the treatment of ALS.

change_quote.quote: Following the advisory committee meeting, the Applicant submitted several new analyses to the NDA that it felt were capable of potentially serving as confirmatory evidence.

summary: The Peripheral and Central Nervous System Drugs Advisory Committee (PCNS) was convened twice for RELYVRIO (AMX0035). On March 30, 2022 it voted 6-4 that the available data were not sufficient to establish effectiveness in ALS; in response the applicant submitted a major amendment with additional confirmatory-evidence analyses (extending the review three months), and the committee was reconvened on September 7, 2022 and voted 7-2 in favor of approval. The AdComm was focused on effectiveness rather than safety, and its first negative vote directly prompted the applicant's submission of new confirmatory evidence that ultimately supported approval; no boxed warning, REMS, or population restriction was tied to the committee's concerns (the imposed PMRs were clinical-pharmacology and nonclinical studies unrelated to the AC).
